reasoning: A graph with 19 vertices, girth at least 8, and every vertex having degree between 4 and 7 is extremely constrained. The Moore bound for graphs with girth g and minimum degree d gives a lower bound on the number of vertices. For girth 8 and degree 4, the Moore bound requires at least 1 + 4*(1 + 3 + 9 + 27) = 1 + 4*40 = 161 vertices for a regular graph. Even for irregular graphs, the cage number for (4,8)-graphs (4-regular, girth 8) is 80 vertices (the Tutte-Coxeter graph has 30 vertices for girth 8 degree 3). With only 19 vertices, it is impossible to have minimum degree 4 and girth 8, because each vertex needs 4 distinct neighbors, each of those neighbors needs 3 more distinct neighbors (not the original vertex), and those need 3 more each, all at distance ≤ 3 from the original vertex without repeating (since girth ≥ 8 means no short cycles). This requires at least 1 + 4 + 4*3 + 4*3*3 = 1 + 4 + 12 + 36 = 53 distinct vertices reachable within distance 3 from any vertex, far exceeding 19. Therefore no such graph exists.
